headline: A 2014 law directs the Forest Service to allow certain existing water facilities inside two Idaho wilderness areas to keep operating and be rebuilt.
what_it_does: The law tells the Secretary of Agriculture to issue a special use authorization for water storage, transport, or diversion facilities on National Forest System land in the Frank Church-River of No Return and Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness areas in Idaho. To qualify, the facility must have existed when the land was designated wilderness and must have been in continuous use delivering water to non-federal land. The owner must also hold a state water right that predates the designation, and relocating the facility must not be practicable or feasible.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of qualifying water facilities inside the Frank Church-River of No Return and Selway-Bitterroot Wildernesses
who_it_affects.how: They can receive a special use authorization to keep operating and rebuild their facilities if they meet all four conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of non-federal land that receives water from these facilities
who_it_affects.how: Their water supply can continue because the facilities serving their land may stay in operation under the authorization.
The agency must issue the required authorizations when the conditions are met.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 25, 2014; the summary does not list a separate effective date.
